concept: Error mitigation can improve noisy hardware evolution results
summary: For circuit-based quantum evolution on noisy hardware or noisy simulators, quantum error mitigation such as readout mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation can improve measured observables or fidelities, but it is a wrapper around a base evolution strategy rather than a replacement for one.
limitations: Does not remove product-formula or Hamiltonian-discretization error.
Requires additional circuit executions and shot budget.
Performance depends on backend noise, observable, extrapolation model, and scaling method.
implications: Recommend error mitigation when the backend is noisy hardware or a noisy simulator and the user cares about measured observables.
Keep the base evolution method recommendation separate from the mitigation wrapper.
Use Mitiq-style zero-noise extrapolation as planned support until implementation and tests exist.

evidence.note: Reports use of readout mitigation and Mitiq-provided zero-noise extrapolation for hardware validation of Trotterized many-body dynamics.
